allies.rationale_text: Scaffolding gives zone-of-development its practical mechanism by shaping the next reachable step instead of demanding mastery in one leap.
allies.source_quote: The scaffolding process is a truly transferable skill applicable in nearly any domain.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical names scaffolding as the primary mechanism of ZOD, breaking problems into parts and providing structured incremental support
allies.activation_condition: When structured, incremental support enables learners to bridge from current competence to the next development level

allies.rationale_text: Systems-thinking is the long-run payoff of zone-of-development because structured learning of parts eventually reveals interrelationships and the big picture.
allies.source_quote: The ZOD model provides the mechanism for acquiring systems thinking.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical lists scaffolding and systems thinking together as the first ally, with ZOD developing capacity for systemic understanding
allies.activation_condition: When ZOD progression develops the capacity to see interrelationships and patterns of change

antagonists.rationale_text: Expertise-reversal-effect undermines zone-of-development by causing experts to skip calibration of challenge to the learner's actual level, communicating at abstractions the learner cannot yet use.
antagonists.source_quote: The Illusion of Understanding (Expert Trap): Expertise can create an illusion of understanding or lead to overconfidence, resulting in an unwillingness to investigate or simplify. Experts often struggle to communicate simply because they naturally want to speak on a higher level of abstraction, leading to the Curse of Knowledge where the message is accurate but useless to the novice.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Expertise reversal occurs when scaffolding structures designed for novices become counterproductive for advanced learners
antagonists.activation_condition: When scaffolding structures become counterproductive for learners who have already internalized the material

structured_tensions.tension_text: Zone-of-development conflicts with status-quo-bias when comfort-zone routines replace stretch-learning progression.
structured_tensions.source_quote: zone-of-development vs status-quo-bias: zone-of-development conflicts with status-quo-bias (status quo bias) when comfort-zone routines replace stretch-learning progression.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Zone-of-development conflicts with authority-bias when rank-based assumptions about instruction block the learner from getting the right growth challenge.
structured_tensions.source_quote: zone-of-development vs authority-bias: zone-of-development conflicts with authority-bias (authority bias) when learner growth is constrained by rank-based instruction assumptions.
